meta.note: Flows resolved latest-year-first (2025>2024), direct report preferred over mirror. Mirror = reconstructed from importer reports; its value is CIF (incl. freight) vs FOB for direct. Metal production is USGS mine production (metric tons of contained metal). Transit routes attribute flows to chokepoints by geography (model estimate) for every commodity; oil pipelines carry crude only.

routes.name: Strait of Hormuz
routes.from: Persian Gulf terminals (Ras Tanura, Kharg, Ras Laffan)
routes.transit_time: Gulf → open sea: ~1 day through the strait
routes.note: The world's most critical oil chokepoint; the only sea route out of the Persian Gulf.

routes.name: Strait of Malacca
routes.note: Shortest sea route between the Gulf/Africa and East Asia; ~2.7 km at its narrowest.

routes.name: Suez Canal & SUMED
routes.transit_time: Canal transit ~12–16 h; Gulf → NW Europe ~15 days
routes.note: Two-way Gulf/Asia ↔ Europe artery for crude and LNG.

routes.name: Bab-el-Mandeb
routes.note: Red Sea gateway; pairs with Suez. Disruriptions here reroute traffic around the Cape.

routes.name: Cape of Good Hope
routes.from: West Africa / Gulf (VLCCs too large for Suez)
chokepoints: Cape of Good Hope (open water, no toll)
routes.transit_time: Gulf → NW Europe via Cape: ~26 days
routes.note: Toll-free deep-water alternative when tankers are too large for Suez or when the Red Sea is avoided.

routes.name: Panama Canal
routes.to: Pacific → East Asia, West coast Americas
routes.transit_time: Canal transit ~8–10 h; US Gulf → Japan ~25 days
routes.note: Key for US LNG and crude heading to Asia and the Pacific coast; capacity-constrained for LNG carriers.

routes.name: Turkish Straits
routes.transit_time: Straits transit ~1 day; frequent congestion delays
routes.note: Sole outlet for Black Sea oil exports (Russia, Kazakhstan, Azerbaijan).

routes.name: Danish Straits
routes.note: Exit for Russian Baltic crude exports into the North Sea.

routes.name: Strait of Gibraltar
routes.note: Atlantic ↔ Mediterranean gateway for cargoes into Southern Europe.

routes.name: Lombok Strait
routes.note: Deep-water bypass to Malacca for the largest tankers bound for East Asia.

routes.name: Druzhba Pipeline
routes.note: One of the world's longest oil pipelines; supplies refineries in Central Europe. (Pipeline crude, not seaborne.)

routes.name: ESPO Pipeline
routes.note: Carries East Siberian crude to Pacific markets and directly to China.

routes.name: Caspian Pipeline (CPC)
routes.note: Kazakhstan's main crude export route; feeds the Turkish Straits onward.

routes.name: Baku–Tbilisi–Ceyhan (BTC)
routes.note: Routes Caspian crude to the Mediterranean, bypassing the Turkish Straits.

routes.name: Keystone Pipeline
routes.note: Primary conduit for Canadian crude into the US market.
